question: In the unsignalized midblock-crosswalk example in Figure 3B-16, how far in advance of the crosswalk are the yield lines shown?
model_answer: Direct Answer: In Drawing B (unsignalized midblock crosswalk) of Figure 3B-16, the yield lines are shown 20 to 50 feet in advance of the nearest edge of the crosswalk. This dimension matches the Guidance in Section 2B.19, which recommends placing yield (stop) lines and Yield Here to (Stop Here for) Pedestrians signs 20 to 50 feet in advance of the crosswalk on an uncontrolled multi-lane approach. Guidance (recommended): - "If yield (stop) lines and Yield Here to (Stop Here for) Pedestrians signs are used in advance of a crosswalk that crosses an uncontrolled multi-lane approach, the signs should be placed 20 to 50 feet in advance of the nearest edge of the crosswalk (see Section 3B.19 and Figure 3B-16)." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 3B-16, Drawing B (unsignalized midblock crosswalk), shows a dimension arrow labeled "20 to 50 ft" between the yield lines (with accompanying R1-5 signs) and the crosswalk; Drawing C (crosswalk across ramp) shows the same 20 to 50 ft dimension. - [Image 4] Page 122 contains the Section 2B.19 Guidance text specifying the 20 to 50 feet placement referenced in Figure 3B-16. - [Image 3] Page 123 shows Figure 2B-2 with the R1-5 series Yield Here To Pedestrians signs that accompany the yield lines depicted in Figure 3B-16. Citations: - Section 2B.19 Guidance §3 (p.81) - Figure 3B-16 (p.574) - Page 122 - Page 123
gold_answer: 20 to 50 feet in advance of the crosswalk.
